speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for sharing your history. Given your symptoms of fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, I need to know if you have experienced any recent infections, travel, or exposure to tuberculosis.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.  
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal. Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): Not available in current data.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I appreciate that information, but a fixed, painless supraclavicular node is highly concerning for malignancy rather than typical tuberculosis. Has the doctor mentioned if you have had any unexplained fevers or if there is a family history of cancer? Please also undergo a biopsy of the lymph node and an ECG immediately. REQUEST TEST: Lymph Node Biopsy; REQUEST TEST: ECG.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lymph Node Biopsy (Cervical Lymph Node): Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. ECG: Not available in current data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index confirms a B-cell malignancy, and the symptoms of weight loss, night sweats, and a fixed supraclavicular node are classic for this condition. Immediate chemotherapy consultation is required.
